figures.title: Holistic Taxonomy of LLM Security Threats
figures.caption: Figure 1: A comprehensive taxonomy of LLM security vulnerabilities categorized by lifecycle stage, distinguishing between training-time exposures, inference-time attacks, and intrinsic model reliability issues.
figures.description: A hierarchical tree diagram branching from 'LLM Security' into three main nodes: Training-Time Threats (Data Poisoning, Generative Backdoors, RLHF Exploitation), Inference-Time Threats (Prompt Injection, Jailbreaking, Adversarial Attacks), and Model Reliability (Hallucinations, Factual Inconsistency).
figures.rationale: The introduction explicitly states the core contribution is a 'holistic taxonomy of LLM security threats'. A visual taxonomy is essential for orienting the reader to the survey's structure.

figures.title: Attack Vectors Across the LLM Operational Lifecycle
figures.caption: Figure 2: Mapping of specific security threats to their corresponding injection points within the LLM development and deployment lifecycle.
figures.description: A sequential flowchart showing the stages: Data Collection -> Pre-training -> Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) -> RLHF -> Deployment/Inference. Red arrows indicate where specific attacks (e.g., Indirect Data Poisoning, BadEdit, BADREWARD, GCG) compromise the pipeline.
figures.rationale: Section 2 emphasizes that vulnerabilities 'permeate the entire model lifecycle'. A flowchart visually reinforces the defense-in-depth concept by showing exactly where the pipeline is vulnerable.

figures.title: Evolution of Backdoor Attack Efficiency: Poisoning Rate vs. Attack Success Rate
figures.caption: Figure 3: Comparison of training-time poisoning attacks. Modern techniques like MABA achieve near-perfect Attack Success Rates (ASR) with sub-1% poisoning rates, demonstrating the increasing stealth and potency of generative backdoors.
figures.description: A scatter plot with 'Poisoning Rate (%)' on the logarithmic X-axis and 'Attack Success Rate (%)' on the Y-axis. It highlights the shift from traditional high-data poisoning to highly efficient modern attacks like MABA (0.2% rate, 97% ASR).
figures.rationale: Directly visualizes the quantitative claim from the text that MABA achieves a 97% success rate with only a 0.2% poisoning rate, illustrating the alarming trend of high-efficiency stealth attacks.

figures.title: Chronological Evolution of Inference-Time Attack Methodologies
figures.caption: Figure 4: The rapid transition from manual heuristic exploits to sophisticated, automated adversarial discovery frameworks between 2023 and 2026.
figures.description: A horizontal timeline plotting key attack methodologies mentioned in the text, showing the progression from manual prompt engineering to gradient-based optimization (GCG) and advanced search algorithms (MCTS Fuzzing/AGENTVIGIL).
figures.rationale: The text explicitly traces the 'chronological evolution of both offensive techniques and defensive mitigation strategies' from 2023 to 2026. A timeline perfectly captures this arms race.

figures.title: Impact of Adversarial Prompts on LLM Reliability in Healthcare Tasks (MIMIC-III)
figures.caption: Figure 5: Degradation of model accuracy when subjected to adversarial attacks on critical healthcare tasks using the MIMIC-III dataset. The stark drop highlights the fragility of unhardened LLMs in clinical settings.
figures.description: A grouped bar chart comparing 'Baseline Accuracy' vs. 'Adversarial Accuracy' across two clinical tasks: 'Vaccination Guidance' and 'Medication Prescription'. The bars show a severe drop in performance under attack.
figures.rationale: Section 5 details a specific evaluation using the MIMIC-III dataset where models show 'substantial decline in accuracy' under attack. Quantifying this 'stark fragility' in a bar chart emphasizes the real-world danger of these vulnerabilities.
